office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Five-term Rep. Jim Walsh, the state Republican Party chair, faces Aberdeen City Councilmember Kevin Moynihan in the coastal and lower-Columbia 19th District. Walsh led the August primary 55.5% to 44.4%.

candidates.summary: Aberdeen publisher first elected in 2016 and state Republican Party chair since 2023; filed the 2023 parents' bill of rights and anti-income-tax initiatives and opposes the 2026 income tax.
highlights: Voted no on ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and offered amendments to it [S7]
Filed the 2023 initiatives on parents' rights (IL-2081), income taxes (IL-2111), police pursuits and cap-and-trade repeal that were certified to the Legislature [S26]
Offered an amendment to restore parental notification rights in ESHB 1296 and voted against the bill [S8][S9]
Led House floor opposition to letting a state commission remove elected sheriffs [S20]
As party chair, quoted in a release stating WAGOP supports enactment of I-645 [S23]

taxes.basis: Voted against ESSB 6346 and the 2025 tax package, calls the income tax unconstitutional, and filed the 2023 no-income-tax and capital-gains repeal initiatives.

spending.basis: Calls for full audits after reported losses of state dollars, ties the income tax to spending growth, voted against the 2025-27 operating budget, and filed spending-growth-limit initiatives.

housing.basis: Voted against the 2025 rent and fee increase limits and the 2026 shelter-siting bill; no affirmative housing plan in the dossier.

safety.basis: Filed police-pursuit and hard-drug initiatives, prefiled a tougher fentanyl-sentencing bill, and opposed state decertification of elected sheriffs.

climate.basis: Voted against the clean fuels program bill and filed initiatives to repeal cap-and-trade.

experience.basis: Five-term incumbent, ranking member on Civil Rights & Judiciary, and state party chair.

local-control.basis: Opposes state removal of elected sheriffs and state limits on local shelter siting; pledges to fight 'unlawful mandates from Olympia.'

immigration.basis: Voted against limits on law enforcement face coverings; session report criticizes pushing sheriffs toward non-cooperation with federal immigration authorities.

parental-rights.basis: Filed the 2023 parents' bill of rights initiative, says parents have a right to notification about school and health information, offered a notification amendment and voted against ESHB 1296.

candidates.summary: Aberdeen City Councilmember, line cook and former HVAC tradesman running on affordability, rent stabilization, rural healthcare and school funding; refuses corporate PAC money.
highlights: Pledges to pass statewide rent stabilization [S1]
Calls for lower prescription drug costs, affordable childcare and more housing [S4]
Wants more funding for rural and coastal schools and competitive educator pay [S4]
Endorsed by the Washington State Labor Council [S9]

housing.basis: Pledges to pass statewide rent stabilization and lists rent stabilization advocacy; also calls for building more housing.

spending.basis: Calls for public investment in ports, schools, childcare and educator pay; no audit or restraint planks.

healthcare.basis: Would protect rural healthcare infrastructure and lower prescription drug costs within the current system; no single-payer position.

experience.basis: City councilmember without legislative service challenging a five-term incumbent; runs as a worker rather than a career politician.

reform.basis: Refuses corporate PAC money and frames his run against 'powerful interests or political insiders.'
